equipment_type: Fan inlet airflow and temperature monitor (airflow measuring station)
applies_to: Ruskin TDFi-Rt thermal dispersion airflow and temperature stations mounted in fan inlets, up to 16 fans.
summary: The TDFi-Rt measures airflow and air temperature at fan inlets with thermal dispersion sensors and reports them over BACnet MS/TP. It exposes only Analog Value objects: a fan summary temperature and airflow, then one temperature and one airflow object per fan for up to 16 fans, plus a Notification Class for alarms. All values are read-only.
notes: AV 3-34 only exist for the number of fans configured: two objects per fan (temperature, then airflow).
Airflow object names change with the display settings: prefix Actual (ACT) or Standard (STD), suffix Velocity or Volume. The names here are the printed defaults.
AV units follow the display settings: °C or °F for temperature; ft/min, m/s, cfm, L/s, L/min, m³/h, ft³/h or ft³/s for airflow.
The device object name and instance are set in the device settings menu; the name can carry the display's line-2 text.

source.title: Advanced Thermal Dispersion Communications for Fan Inlet Air Monitoring (PICS)

integration.summary: A read-only measuring device: set its MS/TP address and baud in the device menu, then read the fan summary airflow and temperature, plus per-fan values if you need them. Choose the airflow units (velocity or volume, actual or standard) on the device before mapping, since the object names and units follow that setting.

minimum_points.name: Fan Summary ACT Airflow
minimum_points.why: Total/average airflow across the monitored fans

minimum_points.name: Fan Summary Temperature
minimum_points.why: Average air temperature across the fans

setup: BACnet MS/TP master at 9600, 19200, 38400 or 76800 baud.
Device instance and name are set in the device settings menu.
Fan count and display units are set on the device; they decide which AV objects exist and their names.
gotchas: Changing the display units renames the airflow objects and changes their units; re-map after any change.
Out_Of_Service is true when a value is not valid, for example during sensor warm-up.
High/low limit alarms are configured through the AV intrinsic reporting properties and the Notification Class object.
